# PR re-review continuation

The review requirements are unchanged: verify prior threads, freshly review every changed file, and publish one `COMMENT` review only after complete coverage.

- Trusted pre-steps capture the PR head/base tip, the immutable PR diff merge base, every changed-file page, complete thread histories and prior reviews, including author and public-timing metadata. One private `ReviewCaptureHost.ps1` session owns policy across changed files, the manifest checkpoint, review history, merge-base validation, baseline inventory and context-export validation. The native adapter retains the caller's injected Octokit client and authentication. The manifest is written before history capture, and the root snapshot is written before export; checkpoint callbacks receive copies, not authoritative state. The diff base supplies old-side source; the base tip remains the freshness anchor. Helpers are checked out before capture. The input artifact is uploaded before inference; workers reuse its review context instead of refetching all review pages in every batch.
- `ReviewContinuation.psm1` owns the worklist, transactional results, ordered pending queue, eight-item/48 KB assignments, retry/backoff, worker instructions/context projection, output construction and shared publication policy. One private `ReviewContinuationHost.ps1` process keeps authoritative state in memory for the entire queue. `ReviewContinuationSession.cjs` provides correlated, bounded stdio and cancellation; `ReviewContinuation.cjs` performs runtime effects and starts fresh CLI sessions using the pinned gh-aw Copilot harness. Independent receipt verification must succeed before the trusted runtime can commit the matching active attempt and nonce. Small patches are embedded; the private input reader pages assigned thread histories and oversized patches. Each response carries a random acknowledgement token; the controller accepts completion only when those tokens match gap-free receipts bound to the captured snapshot, assignment and fresh invocation. `ReviewInputServer.ps1` serves those pages in a pinned glibc container using the checksum-pinned PowerShell runtime in the read-only actions mount. `Export-ReviewContext.ps1` writes the captured context and computes canonical input keys; the server checks page content against those keys before issuing receipts. The trusted adapter validates the snapshot, index and prior-review histories before starting workers. `ReviewVerifyDelivery.ps1` independently recomputes required inputs from the captured snapshot and assigned items using `ReviewSerialization.psm1`, then verifies the resulting ranges and identities. The serializer accepts compact `JSON.stringify` input from the trusted Node adapter; it is not a general JSON formatter. The shared Node supervisor bounds each baseline and context-export process to 22 minutes and handles cancellation and process-group cleanup. Receipts store token hashes, not the tokens. This establishes delivery through the reader, not comprehension.
- Workers use GitHub MCP for source reads and have no shell, write, task or safe-output access. The input-only stdio backend has no GitHub token or HTTP listener. Source reads are model-attested, not independently receipted; if the worker reports required content unavailable, the controller keeps it pending until completion or the deadline. Completed results stay in the private PowerShell host; diagnostic checkpoints are copies and are never reloaded as authoritative progress. Unfinished items continue after a clean early exit. Clean no-progress responses reduce the assignment size but do not terminate review while time remains. Actual worker errors, policy-host protocol failures or the 22-minute soft deadline fail the run. Host failures cancel an active worker or delivery verifier. Final outputs are held until clean host shutdown succeeds; late output, nonzero exit or a shutdown timeout prevents publication. The workflow retains its 25-minute limit.
- Only the controller queues outputs after every item completes. The trusted publication guard checks the Actions job result, immutable input identity, complete results, buffered-output routing, structured coverage counts and current PR/review state. `ReviewBaselines.ps1` fetches and verifies full diff-base/head central ApiCompat baselines through the shared GitHub CLI helper, then compares them once during trusted capture; every new suppression is inventoried independently of worker findings, without asserting that the affected API shipped GA. Publication freshness rereads PR, thread and prior-review state; mutation freshness checks PR state and affected threads without refetching unused reviews or immutable baselines. `ReviewFreshness.ps1` performs the ordered comparisons and applied-reply filtering in a bounded subprocess; trusted publication and mutation jobs require PowerShell 7.3 or later on the runner. Missing or malformed required capture inputs fail closed. Existing threat-detection and skipped-write safeguards remain active. Both resolve and reopen operations wait for proof that the matching reply was applied. Freshness checks and subsequent writes are not atomic; the comparison subprocess can widen that interval. gh-aw remains responsible for sanitizing output text; the publication guard checks the deterministic suppression inventory without reconstructing free-form Markdown.

A completion result is still a model review conclusion, not proof of comprehension. Related-file reads and cross-file review remain required; prior reviews never substitute for a fresh changed-file result. The pinned GitHub MCP tool can fail on files over 1 MiB; an honest unavailable-source result remains incomplete. Source access and review are not independently verified, and this is not an unlimited or resumable-across-workflow-runs service. Ordered retries are preserved: repeated no progress on the first pending item can starve later items until the deadline. The synthetic 106-file regressions do not establish same-model completion within the real controller deadline.

## Runtime boundaries

- PowerShell owns review-policy decisions. Initialization binds the exact compact native `JSON.stringify` snapshot representation; pretty artifact bytes are not an equivalent hash input. Invalid completion batches cannot partially commit.
- The Node continuation bridge retains pinned-harness arguments/event parsing, clean-response normalization, native path resolution and final serialization of the PowerShell-built prompt, asynchronous effects, routing coercion, and POSIX process-group/signal supervision. Its immutable ID bindings and diagnostic copies are not a second pending queue. Workers cannot supply the trusted delivery-verification flag.
- Worker-prompt construction uses the same private queue host and binds the active attempt, nonce, canonical batch and snapshot without committing completion. It adds a request/response round-trip carrying the assigned batch again; large histories/patches therefore incur extra private serialization even though they stay out of the model prompt. Clean-response normalization remains native for now; moving it requires separate protocol and independent-delivery validation.
- The generic session supervisor derives response budgets from actual encoded requests and cumulative successful completion-frame bytes, including generated fields and JSON escaping. It does not impose a new small aggregate result cap or start a policy process per batch/function. Accepted-result and attempt deltas avoid repeatedly transmitting the whole growing checkpoint.
- `ReviewCapture.psm1` owns pagination, exact queries, before/after PR checks, mode-specific review capture, baseline/freshness projections and independent delivery/base/history acceptance. Capture policy failures are terminal; failed drains are never resumed. `ReviewSnapshot.cjs` retains injected-client calls, native JSON/string/scalar encoding and hashes, fixed-path filesystem reads, checkpoint callbacks and the existing bounded helper interfaces. Delivery validation precedes reads; base artifacts are read and validated before histories, and each fixed `review-N.json` is read and validated before the next. Index-claimed paths never select reads.
- The capture-policy process receives an environment stripped of token/secret/password/credential names and SSH/askpass handles. Existing baseline/export helpers retain their parent environment and authentication. Host failure cancels and joins supervised baseline/export teardown before capture settles; injected HTTP reads retain their existing non-abortable semantics. These boundaries are not a universal filesystem sandbox or an HTTP abort guarantee.
- `ReviewDelivery.cjs` retains native snapshot hashing and bounded process supervision for capture and verification. Source/input MCP and receipt adapters retain their native protocol interfaces.
- Test-only pure-policy probes preserve existing synchronous assertions and JavaScript differential oracles. They are not production state or receipt-verification paths.

## Validation

CI provisions the pinned gh-aw setup helpers for handler/receipt tests. PowerShell 7.5 or later must also be on PATH; set `GH_AW_REVIEW_PWSH` to use a specific executable. To run the Node suites locally, point `GH_AW_TEST_ACTIONS_DIR` at those same helpers:

```bash
GH_AW_TEST_ACTIONS_DIR=/path/to/pinned/gh-aw/setup/js node --test .github/workflows/test/*.Tests.cjs .github/workflows/test/pr-re-review-unresolve-thread.test.cjs
```

Run the Pester suites under `.github/workflows/pr-re-review` and `.github/workflows/test`, and compile `pr-re-review.md` with the pinned gh-aw version after workflow changes. Subprocess fixtures reproduce the 106-file clean early-stop case without inference or GitHub writes; they do not establish hosted end-to-end review quality.
